errors.text: The proposed strain-rate range of 10^-4 to 10^2 s^-1 is fundamentally different from the molecular-dynamics regime of 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1, so the claimed rate insensitivity is extrapolated far outside the target boundary.

The hypothesis replaces vacancy-cluster/disordered-atom nucleation sites with unsupported solute clusters or stacking-fault tetrahedra and omits Shockley partials and intrinsic/extrinsic stacking faults as the actual plasticity mediators.

A broad distribution of thermally activated barriers is asserted to explain strain-rate insensitivity, although thermally activated nucleation ordinarily produces rate dependence unless a specific limiting argument is demonstrated.

The cited evidence does not validate the proposed mechanism: E1 concerns a compositionally modified polycrystalline alloy, E2 reports strength increasing with strain rate, and E3 concerns a BCC refractory HEA.
